translationRepairs: The reading runs, 『Kings take it as ill-omened; the sovereign's life is unbounded; a ruler is displaced; one may become king in his stead; the realm changes its dynastic reckoning.』
The reading runs, 『Kings take it as ill-omened; the sovereign's allotted fate has no set term; a ruler is displaced; one may become king in his stead; the realm changes its dynastic reckoning.』
In this ill-omened reading, 主命無期 means the ruler's mandate or allotted span has no secure term, matching 有徙主 and 天下更紀; 'life is unbounded' reverses that sense.
the second year of Jianyuan, ninth month, jiawu new moon: the sun was eclipsed.
In the second year of Jianyuan, ninth month, jiawu new moon: the sun was eclipsed.
The unit is a standalone sentence opening the eclipse series; the lowercased start is ungrammatical, and prefixing In matches neighboring dated entries without changing meaning.
the fourth year of Jianyuan, seventh month, wuchen: the moon was eclipsed in the Wei asterism.
In the fourth year of Jianyuan, seventh month, wuchen: the moon was eclipsed in the Wei asterism.
The unit begins a new sentence and must be capitalized; adding In restores grammar without altering 建元四年七月戊辰 or 危宿.
In the second month of year 6, on the renchen jia watch, the thirteenth jia watch, and the fifteenth jia watch, the moon each time haloed Taiwei.
In the second month of year 6, on the renxu jia watch, the thirteenth jia watch, and the fifteenth jia watch, the moon each time haloed Taiwei.
The date graph is 壬戌 (renxu); renchen would require 壬辰, so the original sexagenary name is wrong.
Year 6, second month—on nights of renchen-jia, the thirteenth jia night, and the fifteenth jia night, the moon all showed halos encompassing Taiwei.
Year 6, second month—on nights of renxu-jia, the thirteenth jia night, and the fifteenth jia night, the moon all showed halos encompassing Taiwei.
The same 壬戌 must be romanized renxu in the literal field; renchen misidentifies the day.
Eighth month, on renshen, the moon stood in the Net, three cun northwest of the second star of the left thigh.
Eighth month, on renshen, the moon stood in the Net and encroached three cun northwest of the second star of the left thigh.
The source verb is 犯, a recorded encroachment on the Net's left-thigh star; locating the moon three cun northwest without that verb omits the omen.
Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the secondary prime minister star below Room's northern head—an encroachment.
Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the second minister star at Room's northern head—an encroachment.
房北頭第二次相星 names the 次相 star at Room's northern head; 次相 is the second-minister title, not a star placed 'below' the head.
Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the secondary prime minister star below the northern head of Room, counted as encroachment.
Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the second minister star at the northern head of Room, counted as encroachment.
The literal field repeats the same invented 'below'; 次相 is the star-title at 房北頭, so 'at the northern head of Room' is the accurate locative.
On bingchen the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at Room's northern end, encroaching.
On bingshen the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at Room's northern end, encroaching.
The source day is 丙申 (bingshen), consecutive after 乙未; bingchen would be 丙辰 and is not in the text.
On bingchen, the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at the northern end of Room, encroaching.
On bingshen, the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at the northern end of Room, encroaching.
The literal date must follow 丙申 as bingshen; bingchen is a different sexagenary day.
In the ninth month, on yichou, the moon occulted Lead Ox's south star.
In the ninth month, on yichou, the moon occulted Ox Leader's south star.
牽牛 is the Ox Leader lodge; nearby units already use Ox Leader for the same asterism, while Lead Ox is a conflicting invented name.
September, on yichou—the moon occulted Lead Ox's south star.
Ninth month, on yichou, the moon occulted Ox Leader's south star.
九月 is the lunar ninth month, not Gregorian September, and 牽牛 should be Ox Leader, not Lead Ox.
September, on gengyin—the moon traveled six cun southwest of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.
Ninth month, on gengyin—the moon traveled six cun southwest of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.
九月 is the ninth lunar month of the chronicle; rendering it as September imports a Gregorian month the source does not use.
Taoyuan 1, seventh month: the moon occulted Heart's middle star.
Taiyuan 1, seventh month: the moon occulted Heart's middle star.
泰 is tài, so 泰元 romanizes as Taiyuan; Taoyuan does not match the graph 泰.
Taoyuan year 1, seventh month—the moon occulted the middle star of Heart.
Taiyuan year 1, seventh month—the moon occulted the middle star of Heart.
The literal field likewise misreads 泰元 as Taoyuan; Taiyuan is the correct transcription of 泰元.
